newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's chemical fibre maker plans B share offer.
newsitem.headline: China's chemical fibre maker plans B share offer.

text.p: Henan-based Xinxiang Chemical Fibre Co Ltd aims to issue 150 to 180 million B shares by the end of this year, a company spokesman said on Friday.

The company, which is among the 33 domestic enterprises newly selected by the securities authorities as candidates for B share listings, has not decided whether to apply to list the stock in Shenzhen or Shanghai, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The precise scale, timing and pricing of the offer have not yet been fixed and the firm is in the process of choosing an underwriter and an international coordinator, the official said.
The company plans to use the proceeds to finance a project capable of turning out 10,000 tonnes of viscose silk a year, the official said.
He said the company expected a 1996 net profit of about 30-40 million yuan, sharply down from some 60 million yuan the previous year.
The firm's operations were heavily affected by the sluggishness that characterised China's textile market thoughout 1996, the official said. He declined to comment on 1997 profits.
